# Frontend design direction — anti-generic design guidance

Curated by Skill Harbor — @affaan-m's frontend design-direction skill: before coding, choose a deliberate direction — the interface's purpose, its audience, an explicit tone (utilitarian, editorial, playful, industrial, refined…), one memorable detail, and the real constraints (framework, accessibility, performance, existing design system) — then build the actual usable experience as the first screen. It pushes the agent to reuse existing components, tokens and routing before inventing a visual system, prefer contextual typography over oversized hero text, keep palettes multi-dimensional, use motion sparingly but deliberately, and verify text fit on mobile and desktop. The anti-pattern list is the point: no purple gradients, decorative blobs, oversized cards, vague hero copy, stock-like media, or cards-inside-cards. Ends with a review checklist (first viewport communicates the product, hierarchy supports scanning, contrast holds, responsive dimensions are stable). Honest caveats: salvaged from a stale community PR (#1659) — the file itself says to install the official Anthropic `frontend-design` skill for the canonical upstream version (see the `anthropics-claude-code-frontend-design` listing); the skill lives under the repo's Japanese docs path (docs/ja-JP/…) though the content is in English. MIT licensed. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
